newsitem.title: FRANCE: France concerned over slaying of Hutus in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: France concerned over slaying of Hutus in Burundi.

text.p: France on Wednesday denounced last week's slaying by Burundian troops of more than 120 Hutu refugees who had returned home from Tanzania and urged that steps be taken to prevent future slaughters.

"This incident is very serious. We have asked our ambassador to inform the Burundian authorities of our deep concern. We expect steps to be taken to prevent a repetition of such events," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.

Tens of thousands of Burundian Hutus have been forced back to their country, ruled by an army dominated by minority Tutsis which the United Nations has blamed for the deaths of hundreds of Hutu returnees in recent months.

In the latest massacre, a Burundian army spokesman said troops shot dead 126 Hutu refugees expelled from Tanzania who tried to escape from a detention centre in Burundi on Saturday. Seven soldiers alleged to have participated were arrested.

Some 220,000 Burundian Hutu refugees remain in Tanzania, and the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR has urged Tanzania to stop forcing them home to Burundi, where the army is at war with Hutu rebels.
